prerequisites: Knowledge of software-engineering aspects such as class diagrams, inheritance, contract-based software design.
Developing and implementing relatively simple algorithms such as Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm.

learning_outcomes.text: Gain deeper insight into the practical application of principles and concepts underlying object-oriented programming.
Learn to develop more complex algorithms based on predefined constraints regarding performance, accuracy, etc.
Gain a better understanding of the impact of quality factors (or non-functional requirements) on the development of software systems, such as adaptability, reusability, and robustness.

Learn to work efficiently in groups and become familiar with functions such as group coordinator (planning, collaboration) and group secretary (document management). Utilize skills such as reporting, presenting, brainstorming, and critically evaluating one's own project.

Acquire a good 'Research & Development' (R&D) attitude, proactively searching for relevant algorithms and associated technical and scientific literature to justify the relevance of a particular algorithmic choice.

syllabus_topics: Developing a medium-sized software system that performs various tasks, in groups of 5 to 6 students.
Increasing difficulty of subtasks and more complex tasks for the system.
Designing, implementing, and planning software components.
Research & Development (R&D) aspects, including searching for relevant algorithms and consulting literature to understand algorithm performance in different situations.
teaching_methods: Presentations on specific technology or algorithms
Regular submission of interim reports with feedback from lecturers
assessment_rules: Teams are graded on project objectives (from reports and demonstrations) and the quality of work (correctness, clarity, depth, insight, effectiveness, inventiveness) including the system, demonstrations, reports, and presentations. Individual contributions within a group are differentiated based on activity, reports, demonstrations, presentations, and peer review. The final score may deviate if a student has insufficiently achieved one or more learning objectives, with the technical-scientific quality of the final result being decisive. There is no second examination opportunity.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
